+## v1.1.42 - 2026-10-30
+
+Pictures on every model and every build: GLM-5.3-Flash now reads pictures on AMD GPUs too, Qwen-3.8-Flash-Next
+(CYBER-FROST) reads pictures for the first time, and DeepSeek and MiniMax read them on every setup again. DeepSeek reads
+long first prompts 16-24% faster and its two-GPU tensor-parallel prompts about 1.5x faster on PCs with few CPU cores,
+GLM's automatic prompt chunk is up to 3.4x faster on cards where it chose too small a chunk, and an idle Maya no longer
+keeps a CPU core busy. Against v1.1.41 on our test PCs, an 8K-token DeepSeek prompt
+read about 1.27x faster on one GPU and 1.1x faster with `--tp 2`; decode, and the other models' speeds, are unchanged.
+
+- **Pictures on every model and every build:**
+  - GLM-5.3-Flash reads pictures on AMD GPUs - Linux and Windows, discrete cards and Ryzen AI Max APUs (#345, thanks
+    @Ehco). The encoder's matmuls and attention now add up in float32 on the GPU, so its answers about a picture match
+    the CPU encoder's on AMD (they drifted on a few image patches before) and on NVIDIA's newer cards too.
+  - Qwen-3.8-Flash-Next (CYBER-FROST) reads pictures. The setup downloads its 0.9 GB image encoder (it asks first),
+    and the encoder runs on the GPU in memory the engine lends it while a picture is read: on an 8 GB card the expert
+    cache and, if need be, the draft layer's experts are lent and read back afterwards. On an 8 GB card a picture is
+    read about 3.6x faster than with the CPU encoder; text answers before and after a picture are the same.
+  - DeepSeek reads pictures with the EXL3 quants on V100s too, and the setup says why a PC short of RAM reads text
+    only. A MiniMax setup run again turns pictures on (it kept an earlier "off" before). `--no-vision` keeps them off
+    for every model.
+- **DeepSeek:**
+  - Long prompts (#691, thanks @needmorevram): the restore points near the end of a prompt are kept in one read, and
+    a chunk streams only the experts it picks. A fresh 20-30K-token prompt read 16-24% faster on one and on two GPUs
+    in our tests, with the same output. Lending EXL3 chunk buffers from the expert cache and reading host-summed
+    pieces back by DMA are opt-in for now (`MAYA_DS4_EXL3_LEND=1`, `DS4_AR_BACK_DMA=1`).
+  - GGUF `--tp 2`: each GPU of a tensor-parallel pair reads only its own part of an expert from the files - on a PC
+    with few CPU cores its prompts took about two thirds of the time (#670, thanks @speja969 for the measurements).
+  - A slow PCIe link (one expert takes 1 ms or more) streams one expert at a time, and the link is measured on the
+    same stream as the loads, which gave back the decode speed lost on such a PC (#609, thanks @SeriousRising, who
+    found the cause).
+  - A GPU too small for the model's dense weights stops at the start with what it needs, instead of a memory error
+    part way into the load.
+- **GLM:** `--prefill auto` no longer falls back to 768-token chunks when the prestage buffer does not fit whole beside
+  a bigger chunk; on such a card a 19K-token prompt read about 3.4x faster (#673, thanks @pietroMastro92).
+- **An idle Maya stays idle** (#685, thanks @vbooka1 for the measurements): after a minute without a request the
+  engines' CPU-lane threads sleep until the next request wakes them (DeepSeek's used up to 12% of a core doing
+  nothing, now none), and the setup screen and the hardware sampler slow down when nothing runs. The first answer
+  after a quiet spell comes as fast as before.
+- **Settings:** a `MAYA_...` setting in a config's `"env"` now reaches the engine under either of its names (#686,
+  thanks @mgabor3141).
+- **Setup:** a discrete NVIDIA card without Resizable BAR is no longer called "shared with the system" (#671, thanks
+  @speja969).
+- **MiniMax:** a routing id outside the experts ends the request with an error that says where, instead of a crash.
+

commit.message:
[Engine] SYCL: the prompt attention batch is budgeted where it is allocated, and stays 32 by default

The scratch of the FP32 prompt attention is batch x chunks x n_head x 258 floats (about 0.41 GB at 32 and 1.65 GB at 128 on
Flash-Next), independent of the prompt chunk.  Prefill::init allocated it from STRATA_ATTN_BATCH (128 since 09524eb47) while the
estimate that sizes the expert cache and the prompt path's loan (bytes_needed_impl) still counted 32, so about 1.2 GB was never
reserved and a single 32 GB Arc Pro B65 with the config setup writes failed its first request ("device buffers for a chunk of 512
tokens do not fit (2098 of 32656 MiB free)").  Both now use one function (attn_batch_for), and the batch is capped at the chunk's
token count, since a chunk never runs more queries than it has.

The default goes back to 32: with the budget honest, 128 would take 1.2 GB from the expert cache on every Intel card for a
1.1-1.3% faster prompt on two B65s.  STRATA_ATTN_BATCH still sets it (1..1024), and is now counted.

data.title: CPU lane: IQ1_M rows with folded scales and int16 sums, IQ2_XS one-token own rows (bit for bit ggml-cpu dot)
data.body:
**What.** `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2.cpp` (`row_dot_iq1m`, `row_dot_iq2xs`, `iq256_rows1_supported`), on top of #452's rows:

- **IQ1_M.** A microbenchmark showed #452's rows are bound by the total uop count (Broadwell: 4 a cycle, ~20 cycles per 64 weights), not by the shuffle port. Two exact integer identities cut the uops:
  1. IQ1_M grid bytes are only -1 / 0 / +1, so `maddubs(|g|, sign(q8, g))` equals `maddubs(scale, sign(q8, g))` with the block scale folded in, and both `|g|` sign ops go.
  2. Scales 2s + 1 <= 15 go into maddubs' unsigned operand. A lane is at most 2 x 15 x 128 = 3840, and 8 of them a block at most 30720, which fits int16. So the sums accumulate in int16, with **one `madd` a block** instead of 4 `madd` + 4 `add` per 64 weights.

  Grid indices come from ggml's `pdep` form where `pdep` is fast (CPUID: BMI2, and not AMD / Hygon below family 19h), elsewhere from scalar indices into a 4-entry table. The delta signs come from one broadcast of qh, with no `set_epi64x`. The int32 lanes per block are ggml's exact integers, and ggml's float steps are unchanged.
- **IQ2_XS.** The grid by `tab4` from scalar u16 loads, half-scales from a 256-entry table. Its one-token own rows are enabled (type 17 in `iq256_rows1_supported` / `iq256_rows1`); before, IQ2_XS at one token fell back to ggml's `vec_dot`.
- No AVX2 code runs before `main`: the tables are `constexpr` (`.rodata`), and the `pdep` probe is a function-local static behind `cpu_avx2_ok()`, so a pre-AVX2 CPU still reaches the ggml fallback.
- Tests: `native_rows_exact_test` gains the IQ1_M int16 worst case (every scale 15, an all +1 grid, every delta bit, q8 = -127, lanes at +-30480). `ds4_lane_bench` gains an `iq2_xs` format and prints the exactness of each format's one-token and multi-token rows.

**Setting:** `DS4_IQ1M_PDEP=0/1` forces the index form on a BMI2 CPU, for checking the other form (both exact); unset = the CPUID choice above. A row in `docs/SETTINGS.md`, beside `DS4_IQ1_PDEP`.

**Overlap with #584** (open): #584 sends one-token IQ1_M rows to ggml-cpu's own BMI2 dot where `pdep` is fast. This PR touches the same routing: our rows are faster than ggml's dot at one token (table below) and also cover several tokens, which #584 leaves alone. If #584 lands first, this replaces its one-token routing with these rows and would keep its `cpu_pdep_slow()` probe instead of ours; happy to rebase either way.

| IQ1_M, one 2304 x 5120 matrix, one Broadwell core, L3-resident | ms |
|---|---|
| #452's rows (v1.1.35) | 2.292 |
| ggml-cpu AVX2 + BMI2 dot (what #584 routes to) | 1.269 |
| this PR, `pdep`-free form (chosen on Zen 1/2, Hygon) | 1.402 |
| **this PR, `pdep` form** | **1.152** |

**Output: unchanged**, bit for bit ggml-cpu's dot:

- the engine's start gate is unchanged (`rows_match_ggml`: 306 one-token rows and nt 2/5/11, with the subnormal shifts; any mismatch falls back to ggml); both forms pass it for IQ1_M and IQ2_XS;
- `native_rows_exact_test`: "all identical" with `DS4_IQ1M_PDEP` unset, `=0` and `=1`;
- `ds4_iq1_rows_test` (`DS4_IQ1_PDEP=0` and `=1`, its two CMake tests): 36 cases, 0 differ from ggml-cpu's dot;
- `ds4_lane_bench --check`: IQ1_M and IQ2_XS own rows bit-identical to ggml's dot, one token and several; every format within 1.8e-7 of the double reference;
- `ds4_gguf_test`: ALL OK; the engine run below gives the same token ids and DSpark counts as v1.1.35.

**Measured.** CPU: 16-vCPU Xeon E5-2697 v4 VM (Broadwell, AVX2 + BMI2, 4-channel DDR4-2133), g++ 13.3, `-march=native`. `ds4_lane_bench`, one token, an expert end to end (gate/up/down, activation quant, SiLU, the pool's jobs), v1.1.35's binary vs this branch's, one run each:

| format | 1 thread, v1.1.35 | 1 thread, this PR | 14 threads, v1.1.35 | 14 threads, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IQ1_M | 7.097 ms | **4.199** (1.69x) | 0.757 | **0.387** (1.96x) |
| IQ2_XS | (no `iq2_xs` format in v1.1.35's bench) | 3.522 | | 0.338 |
| IQ2_XXS (code unchanged) | 4.423 | 4.811 | 0.489 | 0.498 |

(IQ2_XXS's code is not changed; its 1-thread difference is run-to-run spread on a shared VM.)

Engine: 2x CMP 170HX 64 GB (sm_80; PCIe Gen2 x16 + Gen2 x4, platform-specific), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 GSQ-RCO IQ2_XXS (routed experts IQ1_M / IQ2_XS / IQ2_XXS; most in VRAM, the rest on the CPU lane), `--tp 1 --gpus 0,1 --dspark on --cpu-threads 14 --suffix-draft 0`, 2000 fixed prompt ids + 256 greedy tokens, one run per binary: verify time 5086.6 -> 4529.6 ms over the same 80 DSpark rounds (**-11 %**), decode 40.68 -> 45.10 tok/s, the same ids. Earlier, through the server on our v1.1.29-based fork (5 prompts x 512 tokens, temperature 0): -6.5 % / -3.8 % a verify window, `--dspark none` -3.1 % / -2.3 % a step, the same text; the larger gain on v1.1.35 was not analysed.

Zen 3 / Zen 4 / newer Intel (the `pdep` form) and Zen 1/2 / Hygon (the `pdep`-free form): not measured. The gain depends on how much CPU-lane time is exposed; a box that streams more experts from RAM should gain more (not measured).

**Checks** (as `.github/workflows/tests.yml`): `tools/check_hip_compat.py` OK; server tests 463 OK (12 skipped); installer and tools tests 584 OK (31 skipped) - the same counts as v1.1.35.
